title: Reflection and Attributes
summary: Programs that look at themselves - Type objects, reading properties and methods with reflection, creating objects and calling methods by name, attributes as labels on code, writing and reading your own attributes, and why source generators replace much of this today.

cards.q: Does an attribute do anything on its own?
cards.a:
No: it is data that some code must read and act on

An attribute is only metadata stored with the code. It has an effect only when the compiler, a framework or reflection code looks for it.

cards.q: Why prefer `nameof(Counter.Add)` to `"Add"` in reflection code?
cards.a:
The compiler checks `nameof`, so a rename updates it or causes a compile error

`nameof` becomes the same constant string at compile time, so it is not faster. The gain is that a typo or rename is caught by the compiler instead of failing at run time.

cards.q: Which call creates an object of a Type t without naming its class in code?
cards.a:
Activator.CreateInstance(t)

Activator.CreateInstance calls the type's parameterless constructor at run time.
